points: Q3 2026 revenue growth will show whether the recent estimate lift is real: the 90-day revenue estimate is up 2.31% and analysts have revised up 13-to-0 in the last 30 days, so the print needs to confirm organic momentum rather than just estimate creep.

The Q3 adjusted EPS result will reveal if CPAY is tracking toward the FY1 consensus of $27.36, roughly 28% growth, and the management-reported 2026 cash EPS midpoint near $27.35; a beat or unchanged trajectory supports the long case.

Corporate payments volume and revenue mix are the central read-through; reports suggest this segment is taking center stage, and Q3 will show if it is accelerating enough to offset any divestiture or portfolio-trimming drag.

Management signaled the Epyx divestiture and more portfolio trimming around the Q2 report, so Q3 updates on timing, proceeds and margin impact will matter for whether the business is becoming simpler and more cash-generative.

Peer prints from JKHY, GPN, NATL, PAYO and EVTC on Nov 3-7 will set sector sentiment before CPAY reports on Nov 10; strong payment-volume and margin commentary supports the long setup, while broad weakness would raise the bar for CPAY to differentiate.

FY2 consensus EPS growth is already expected to slow to about 14% ($31.24), so Q3 guidance will show whether that deceleration is priced in or if growth is fading faster, which is the main risk to the below-theme PEG valuation.
watch: Q3 revenue growth vs the 90-day +2.31% estimate drift and 13/0 up/down revision skew — continued upside supports the long.
